name: 1N5819 Schottky diode, 1 A, DO-41 (through-hole)
blurb: 1 A Schottky diode with about 0.3 to 0.6 V drop, for reverse-polarity protection, OR-ing supplies and motor flyback; current flows from the anode to the banded cathode end.

pins.name: K
pins.note: Cathode: the end with the colour band. Current flows from A to K, so K goes toward the load side when the diode is used for reverse-polarity protection.

pins.name: A
pins.note: Anode: the end without the band. Goes toward the supply.

verify: Body and leads are from the Vishay 1N5817/18/19 drawing (DO-41 / DO-204AL: body diameter 2.0 to 2.7 mm, length 4.1 to 5.2 mm, lead diameter 0.71 to 0.86 mm, leads 25.4 mm min); the larger diameter is drawn. The body is drawn as the envelope of the 10.16 mm lead span, not as the 5.2 mm plastic; the band sits on a 5.2 mm body centred in the span (x 2.48 to 7.68), at x 2.9 to 3.7. 10.16 mm is a fitting pitch (leads bend to 7.62 mm), not a datasheet figure. Lead 25 mm is the datasheet minimum, rounded down. 1N5819 ratings from the datasheet: 40 V repetitive reverse, 1.0 A average forward, 0.60 V forward drop at most at 1 A. The 1N4001 to 1N4007 rectifiers use the same DO-41 outline (general knowledge, not opened) but are slow silicon diodes with about 1 V drop: do not swap them in where the low drop matters.
sources: https://www.vishay.com/docs/88525/1n5817.pdf (opened and read: page 3 DO-204AL outline with body diameter, length, lead diameter and lead length; colour band marks the cathode; 1N5819 VRRM, IF(AV), VF)
